messages:
maria: Quick question about the console UX for route matching precedence — I keep getting tripped up by header anchors vs host globs. Can we add an inline hint in the route editor? :thinking:
kevin: Short answer: header anchors are evaluated after exact host matches but before host wildcards when the header is explicitly anchored to a service. This is by design to let ops route by client id header without needing host changes.
olga: Hmm, that ordering feels surprising. Can you show a tiny example?
kevin: Yep. Example config (pseudo):
```
routes:
  - host: api.example.com
    path: /payments/*
    service: payments-v2
  - host: "*"
    header_anchor:
      header: x-client
      value: internal
    service: internal-proxy
```
Here an exact host+path wins first. If host is wildcard, the header-anchored rule kicks in before other wildcard hosts.
ben: If we add this to the console, we should show a one-line hint under the rule: "Evaluation order: exact host -> host + header anchors -> host wildcards -> regex captures". But that wording might be too prescriptive.
alice: Could we instead show a small visual preview: given an example request (host, path, headers) the editor shows the matched rule? That would make precedence obvious and testable.
maria: Love the preview idea. Lightweight: inputs for host/path/headers and a green highlight of matched rule. No infra changes to matching logic.
kevin: Implementation note: preview must use the same matcher code path as runtime (no separate heuristics). Otherwise it will confuse people. Also limit previews to 100ms so it feels snappy in the UI.
olga: On the semantics side — what about regex vs capture patterns? We have a few customers who rely on a regex route that overlaps with a capture route. Which wins today?
kevin: Current rule: exact literal > anchored header > host specificity > path specificity > regex > capture (tie-breakers by creation timestamp). Regex is considered "heavier" and evaluated later so literal/capture gets preference.
ben: That ordering is odd for folks that use regex for very specific matches. Maybe we should allow an explicit `priority` integer on a route to override defaults? That would let power users opt out of the baked ordering.
alice: I worry about adding `priority` — it's another knob that everyone will lean on and then we have unobservable chaos. Maybe we expose `priority` but hidden behind an "advanced" toggle in the console and only editable via API by default.
maria: For the console hint text, can we avoid deep order table and just show one compact line plus a "why" link to docs? e.g., "Match precedence: literal host+path → header anchors → host globs → regex → captures (advanced: priority)".
kevin: Works for me. Also: we should clarify how header overrides interact with rollouts. If a header-anchored rule points at a canary service, and a later rule points to stable, we should show the rollouts badge in the preview.
olga: Good call. Also add a small CTA: "Test request against live canary" that runs in sandbox mode so we don't hit prod backends.
deploy-bot: deploy 1758128 by kevin: route-editor-hints UI deployed to staging :rocket:
ben: After staging smoke, open a tiny A/B with 10% of edits showing the preview to users and measure help-clicks vs revert rate?
maria: Action items: 1) kevin to PR console hint line + preview mockups, 2) alice to design advanced priority toggle copy, 3) olga to draft docs snippet showing ordering + examples, 4) ben to plan lightweight experiment.
kevin: I'll put up the PR today and link the mock in the thread. :thumbsup:
thread_text: Quick discussion about console hints and precedence for header-anchored rules vs host globs, with example config and UI preview proposal. Action items listed.
